article.title: Reuters' 21 October IBM report: software revenue growth outlook and the deal-timing test
article.dek: Reuters reported a higher lower bound for IBM's annual software revenue growth outlook on 21 October 2026. Its account of deferred deals leaves a question about repeatable demand.
article.substack_body_markdown:
Reuters reported on 21 October 2026 that IBM's annual software-revenue growth outlook was about 7% to 8%, compared with 6% to 8% previously. The reported revision raised the lower bound and left the upper bound unchanged. How much of the quarter reflected fresh business, and how much depended on transaction timing? [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

Reuters put third-quarter total revenue at $17.10 billion, with software revenue of $7.80 billion. These are quarterly results as reported by Reuters; the annual growth range is management's expectation. Software revenue is included in IBM's total revenue. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

Kavanaugh told Reuters that approximately 25% of transaction-processing revenue reflected deals postponed from the second quarter; he described the other 75% as new business. Both percentages refer to transaction-processing revenue. The split distinguishes delayed deals from new business within that revenue category. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

If Reuters' account is accurate, delayed transactions contributed to the quarter alongside new business. That gives two possible explanations for the reported improvement: stronger ongoing demand and a recovery in the timing of deals. The raised lower bound remains management's expectation; the reported quarter alone cannot establish how durable any improvement would be. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

The next useful test is whether further reported results substantiate the new-business explanation. More detail on the contribution from deferred transactions would help distinguish deal timing from repeatable demand. The 21 October 2026 report does not establish that subsequent outcome. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade. Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]
article.social_hook: Reuters' 21 October IBM report described a higher lower bound for annual software-revenue growth. The deal mix leaves the useful question: how much growth can repeat?
